Every public appearance of mine was useful for all of us because it was a way of motivating people all over the world to help us and so did this public appearance of mine. But even after this, we did admit people and granted them refugee status which is a fact that can be verified easily.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can be provided with the Prlic Defence binder, if I can have the assistance of the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you have that, sir, can you please turn to 1D 02606. Again, if you can't find it, please let me know. My apologies, that's not the right one. Give me a moment, please. 2607, my apologies. 2607. My staff has corrected me, Your Honour. 2608. 2608. I'm not sure how that happened but ... Dr. Zoric, if you can bear with me, please, and if you can find 2608. Now, this is a letter written later that I think may have been shown to you during the Defence questioning dated the 29th of October, 1992, concerning what's been referred to and what is referred to here as a "one-time financial assistance." Now, if I can direct your attention, please, to paragraph numbered 1, it says, "To strictly obey" -- they ask the regional offices "To strictly obey the stipulations of the Government of the Republic of Croatia as regards approving or non-approving the refugee status to those refugees who have arrived to Croatia before July 13, 1992." And isn't it a fact, sir, that that date continued to be a very important date that persons who had arrived before the 13th of July, 1992, could receive refugee status and those who arrived after the 13th of July, 1992, were not given refugee status?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, before he answers the question, I would ask that the Prosecutor read the rest of that paragraph or I can read it for him. "It is because there have been some irregularities." I think it's within that context. So maybe now he can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My question, Dr. Zoric, is the same: Isn't it correct that persons who arrived before July 13th, 1992, and assuming they could otherwise meet the criteria, those persons who arrived before that date were granted refugee or could be granted refugee status, but persons who arrived after that date were not granted that status?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Persons who arrived later could also be granted that status. It is difficult for me to say which irregularities are specifically being referred to but we tried to prevent people from getting that status if they were not entitled to it such as forging documents to be included and the -- in aid schemes or people who were from areas not affected by the war. I believe that this is what Dr. Rebic means by irregularities but Croatia did grant refugee status even after that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'll refer you back to your testimony a moment ago and as reflected in part or at least as consistent with the Reuters news article, "As of the 13th of July, 1992, Croatia announced that it would grant no more persons refugee status." That statement said nothing about irregularities, it said that, we will no longer accept and take refugees. Isn't it -- I go back to my question, sir. After -- persons arriving after the 13th of July, 1992, were not given refugee status; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object on the grounds that it's been asked and it's been answered. The gentleman did indicate that they were granted, now he can accept it, he can accept that answer or not. Now, I don't mind him asking it again but I believe that Mr. Zoric has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, he answered -- he gave an answer and then he changed his answer with the reference to the irregularities. A few moments ago, he said, he agreed with me that on the 13th of July, 1992, there would be no more refugees. Then now he said, well, based upon something about irregularities, and that's not what he said previously so I'm trying to come back and clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect and I understand that under cross we can get a little excited but --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't need to be lectured by Mr. Karnavas, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not lecturing the gentleman. He was pointed to one document. He indicated, yes, that's what it says, however, we continued to provide status to them. That was his answer. It's in the record. He was then asked again and he was pointed to this document. I asked for purposes of completion, in fairness to the gentleman, that it be put into context. Now, the question can be asked again one more time and let the gentleman give an answer but I don't think that there is an inconsistency, and the record speaks for itself. It's in the record. I don't wish to complicate matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't think there was anything unclear about my question but let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- state it again, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You appeared to add, if I heard you correctly, you appeared to comment a few moments ago that refugee status was stopped as of the 13th of July, 1992, and then I think I heard you say that at some point in time in the future, it was granted again; that is, people were given that status beginning at some future time. Now, if that's your answer, and we'll come back to that in a moment if he we need to, but if that's your position, can you tell us when refugee status began once again to be granted to persons arriving from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is difficult for me to provide an answer now, but I am sure that there is extensive documentation to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm going to have to ask you to do your best. You've answered extensive questions on behalf of Defence counsel and I want you to do your best to tell us when refugee status was again granted, 1995? 1996? Please assist us.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was that same year that we continued granting refugee status. But I cannot give you an exact date. It would be very difficult for me to do so now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, to turn to, in the Prosecution binder, P 10407. In the Prosecution binder, I think I see you have the right one. Thank you. Sir, this is a letter or a communication signed at least over the name of Mr. Rebic who we've talked about extensively in the last day and a half. And did you have -- looking at this document, did you have occasion to see communications like that or perhaps to even prepare some similar communications yourself prior to the time that you became a member of parliament?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen similar documents. This is a document by which the office gave its approval to anyone to stay in Croatia temporarily but that somebody did not apply for refugee status.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, this is dated the 9th of April, 1993 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, I was told that this document is not part of the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour. I'll have to ask Ms. Winner. It should be. Our records show that it is. If you want me to provide you with hard copy, I can do that but -- or we can put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't find it either so we're having the same problem. Is it 10407? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: 10407. So I don't have a clean copy I'm afraid. Can someone provide me with a clean copy. If we can look on the ELMO, sir, and I'll just indicate that, and everyone in the courtroom I'm sure will correct me if I'm wrong, this is a letter as I mentioned the a moment ago dated the 9th of April, 1993, and I'm directing your attention to the second page. In connection with these individuals, the letter makes a very specific reference to -- that while these persons will be allowed to come into the country, "Pursuant to the decision of the government of the Republic of Croatia of 13 July 1992, the above mentioned persons cannot request or be granted a refugee status in the Republic of Croatia."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, this is April 1993, some nine or ten months after that decision and that decision, sir, continued to be in effect and was still used to deny people refugee status in Croatia for a long period of time; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We must bear in mind that Croatia already has around 300.000 displaced persons as Croatian citizens and 300.000 refugees which makes a total of 600.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you not tell me whether it was good or bad will or how many people were in Croatia. We've all understood that there was a lot of people coming from Bosnia-Herzegovina into Croatia. I don't question that. You needn't remind me of that. This document says that these two individuals be allowed to come into the country but the letter is very clear and explicitly stating that according to the law dated 13 July 1992, they will not be granted refugee status; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, Mr. Prosecutor, this document reads that these persons from Jablanica wanted to go to Zagreb for some reason, that somebody sent them an invitation from Zagreb, and the details are mentioned here, the address. As far as I know, Jablanica was controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina during the whole war. I don't see why anybody should be a refugee fleeing from their own army. These persons asking for this permission were Bosnian Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Scott. Witness, the Prosecutor asks you so-called directive questions. That is something he's allowed to do. And they are questions which call for an answer, yes or no. I have followed this and I do not think that one single time you have actually answered the question. Every time, you took the floor, you started an excursion upon some kind of explanation. I can very well understand your urge to do this and I have had an experience, it's the same with me. Unfortunately, these rules are rather strict and we lose quite an amount of time because you do not, for reasons that I really understand, but you do not conform -- confirm to this rule and that makes the task for the Chamber more difficult than would -- than it is anyway. So if I may ask you to respect these rules, we would be very grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, just to clarify so we can go forward, so that we have your answer. You're telling the Trial Judges under oath that you did not consider Jablanica in 1993 to be a war area?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me, excuse me. He's mischaracterizing the evidence. He said it was controlled under the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that's number one. Number two, there's nothing here to suggest that they were requesting and that they were denied. We don't know why they wanted to go to Croatia and go to some place else but I think that Mr. Scott is assuming facts which are not in evidence. The document is what it is, but I don't think that we can say that somehow they were -- they were -- they asked for refugee status or they were denied but they were merely given this permit to go through. So he needs to lay a predicate. And I don't think that we can conclude -- we cannot conclude from the second paragraph that there was a request and that there was a denial. I don't see that in the facts, and perhaps I can be assisted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with the concept that -- during the time that you were associated with these issues were you familiar with a concept of someone obtaining a so-called letter of guarantee and a transit visa, some permission to travel or pass through or to the Republic of Croatia or is that a completely new concept to you?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you say, sir, that in the first page of this document that it says, right under the subject and et cetera, "The Office for Refugees and Displaced Persons of the government of Croatia agrees to allow entry and temporary residence for the following persons ..." it gives the names of the individuals, the place from which they will travel, Mostar, "The above-mentioned person will be provided with full financial support and accommodation by the following individual." One could take that in the light of what we've come to understand as the guarantee and then the Rebic letter goes on to make it very clear, however, that while that will be allowed, we want to make it very clear these persons are not being given refugee status. Now that's what the letter says; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR ZORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And wasn't that in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Witness, I'm following carefully and reading carefully this letter. Mr. Rebic will testify as well, and we will be able to put him questions but Mr. Karnavas is very right when he says that nothing tells us in this letter that these people requested a refugee status. There is no evidence to that effect. They did not ask for a refugee status even if, in the last sentence, it says that, "In accordance with the decision of the 13th of July 1992, the above-mentioned people would not receive a refugee status." I notice that this document has to be shown at the checkpoint and I wondered the following: So we have these two people, they live in Mostar, because we see that they are from Mostar. They want to go to Zagreb. And somebody will put them up and it's the name of the person that appears here. So they want to live in Zagreb for a certain amount of time but we don't know how much. I would like to know if the office was capable of giving these types of temporary documents for these people to stay in Croatia. Because look at the memo under subject, there is reference to a temporary residence. So these people will -- would not stay in Croatia for the rest of their lives. I would just like to know if this office was authorised to deliver temporary permits to foreigners who wanted to come and spend some time in Zagreb. People who had a certificate such as this one but who would never obtain a refugee status and that in order to allow them to cross the border they had to show this document at the checkpoint. I would like to know if this is something that you are familiar with, if what I'm describing to you is exactly how it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think you're entirely right. The office declares here that they've received the letter of guarantee from someone in Zagreb. The office also declares itself willing to have this person arrive in Croatia; however, the office also claims that nothing was sought from it. Therefore, these do not constitute sufficient reasons to grant refugee status. The office had no power over the border police. The office simply said that it would in no way oppose the arrival of those persons. The office, however, also stated that they didn't believe those people should be recognised as refugees and that was as far as its remit went. Had the documents shown been different, the reply by the office would also probably have been a different one. I don't know to what extent people are familiar with language issues here, but this is in the passive voice, not in the active voice. The office agrees that entry should be granted. It's not about the office itself granting entry, it's about the office agreeing that access or entry should be granted which means that a suggestion is being made to whoever is in charge. We in no way oppose this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We shall stop here because it is the end of our working day. We will resume tomorrow at 9.00 a.m. I wish you all a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th of May, 2008 at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
